decisions.question: Are your multiple-choice answers about sound final, or starting priors that blind A/B listening on the hand-written loops then settles?

options.label: Answers are final
options.consequence: Fastest Phase 1, but values picked in words (MPC 58%, rain at -24 dB) may not be what your ears prefer.

options.label: Answers set a range, blind A/B picks the value
options.consequence: Example: swing 54 vs 58 vs 62, or rain -24 vs -18, on 2-3 hand loops. About 1-2 h, and the rating UI must exist by about Nov 5.

options.label: Every palette constant settled by a blind A/B tournament
options.consequence: Most faithful to your ear. About 3-5 h of listening squeezed into Nov 2-8.

decisions.question: What is the loop's main job?

options.label: Background for focus (study or work)
options.consequence: Caps note density and lead prominence, keeps bar 8 unsurprising, favors sparse steady loops.

options.label: Mood piece (rainy-night atmosphere)
options.consequence: Bed and reverb more prominent, slow harmony, lead optional.

options.label: Head-nod groove
options.consequence: Drums and bass forward, motif repetition welcome, looser density caps.

options.label: Varies per brief
options.consequence: The job becomes a brief knob. The RM, density caps and knob obedience must all take it into account.

decisions.question: Which lineage sets the default sound?

options.label: Jazzhop (Nujabes / J Dilla)
options.consequence: 80-100 BPM, 9th to 13th chords, Rhodes, sax, flute or vibes, layered swing, light crackle.

options.label: Study beats / chillhop (Lofi Girl)
options.consequence: 70-90 BPM, soft drums derived from boom-bap with rimshots and shakers, jazzed-up I-vi-ii-V, cleaner sound.

options.label: Sleepy / ambient lo-fi
options.consequence: 55-80 BPM, brushes or no drums, 2-4 slow chords, understated melody, steady noise floor.

options.label: Dusty 90s boom-bap
options.consequence: 85-96 BPM, hard kick, swung hats, 12-bit grit, sine-like bass doubling the roots.

decisions.question: Does one sound serve every brief, or can a brief pick a second style?

options.label: One style for all briefs (as planned)
options.consequence: Every vote compares like with like. Least audition and licensing work.

options.label: One palette with 2-3 presets the brief can pick (tempo, mix, swing)
options.consequence: More variety, but the pair sampler must match presets and the RM sees the preset as a confound.

options.label: Two full sub-palettes (e.g. jazzhop and sleepy)
options.consequence: Doubles audition and licensing work, gives each style about half of the ~1,500 votes, and needs a change to CLAUDE.md section 8.

decisions.question: What is the tempo policy, given that the model never writes tempo?

options.label: One fixed tempo (e.g. 80 BPM, so every loop is 24.0 s)
options.consequence: A/B toggling synced to the bar is trivial, and tempo never confounds votes. Least variety.

options.label: Small fixed set the brief picks from (e.g. 72/80/88)
options.consequence: Loops last 26.7, 24.0 or 21.8 s. You can only toggle between same-tempo pairs, and LFO periods are recomputed per tempo.

options.label: Continuous band the brief picks from (e.g. 70-90)
options.consequence: Most variety, but pairs are rarely the same length and the RM must learn to ignore tempo.

decisions.question: The model writes scale degrees but never the key. Who sets the tonic and the mode?

options.label: One fixed key and mode (e.g. D Dorian)
options.consequence: No key confound, and registers and sample zones are the same everywhere. But every loop has one tonal color, which may tire you over 1,500 votes.

options.label: Fixed tonic, brief picks the mode (Aeolian, Dorian, Ionian, Lydian)
options.consequence: Mode becomes a strong mood knob. The chord vocabulary and verifiers must be mode-aware.

options.label: Brief picks the tonic from 3-4 keys, mode fixed
options.consequence: Transposing moves SoundFont sample zones and register clamps, and key becomes a nuisance variable for the RM.

options.label: Brief picks both tonic and mode
options.consequence: Most variety, most confounds, and the largest audition matrix.

decisions.question: How much swing per layer, in MPC % (50 is straight, 54 loosens without sounding swung, 66 is about triplet, 75 is the maximum)?

options.label: Everything straight (50)
options.consequence: Tight and quantized, the clean chillhop end. Nothing to tune.

options.label: Light, the same on every layer (54-58)
options.consequence: Loose but coherent. The even 16ths land 15-30 ms late at 80 BPM.

options.label: Split: kick and snare 8th-note swing about 57, hats 16th-note swing 62-74
options.consequence: The shape of Attack's boom-bap recipe (57/74): lazy hats over a steady backbone.

options.label: Heavy, the same on every layer (62-66)
options.consequence: Shuffle or jazz feel. The even 16ths land 40-69 ms late at 70-90 BPM.

decisions.question: Where does swing live?

options.label: Frozen palette constant
options.consequence: The model can't change it, so votes judge composition only. You set the feel once, by ear.

options.label: Brief knob
options.consequence: Adds variety and a knob-obedience target. The RM must treat feel as a covariate.

options.label: Bounded field the model writes in LoopScript (e.g. 50-66)
options.consequence: The RM can teach the model your feel, but it widens the hack surface and votes mix feel with composition.

decisions.question: On top of swing, should some drum layers sit at fixed early or late offsets (the Dilla-style tug between layers)?

options.label: None: every layer on the swung grid
options.consequence: Clean, predictable feel.

options.label: Snare laid back by 10-20 ms
options.consequence: Lazy backbeat, with kick and hats on the grid.

options.label: Clap or snare about 10 ms early, hats late
options.consequence: Tension in the style of 'Get Dis Money'. Drunker.

options.label: Kick and snare well behind the hats (up to a septuplet, about 95 ms at 90 BPM)
options.consequence: Very drunk. Treat it as a feel idea and audition it carefully.

changes: renderer (sample-accurate drums vs FluidSynth ~1.45 ms blocks)

decisions.question: Should the pitched parts (lead, keys) sit behind the beat like a relaxed soloist?

options.label: On the grid
options.consequence: Lead locks to the drums. The most programmed feel.

options.label: Slightly behind (15-30 ms late)
options.consequence: Relaxed. The same offset feels different on soft and sharp sounds, so audition it in context.

options.label: Strongly behind (40-80 ms late)
options.consequence: Jazz-soloist drag (the figure of about 100 ms for soloists is UNVERIFIED). Can come across as late or sloppy.

decisions.question: Should timing and velocity variation repeat exactly every bar, or vary from hit to hit?

options.label: Repeat exactly every bar
options.consequence: Like Dilla's repeated offsets. Loops perfectly, but can sound programmed.

options.label: Small fixed per-hit jitter on all layers (about +/-5-10 ms from a hash PRNG seeded by the loop)
options.consequence: Livelier. No two rendered bars are identical, yet the WAV stays bit-identical.

options.label: Jitter on hats and ghost notes only
options.consequence: Movement on top over a stable kick and snare.

decisions.question: How large is the chord vocabulary?

options.label: 7ths only (maj7, m7, 7)
options.consequence: Safest and plainest.

options.label: Add 9ths (maj9, m9, 9, add9)
options.consequence: Classic lo-fi color.

options.label: Add 11ths and 13ths (m11, 13, maj7#11)
options.consequence: Jazzhop color, with more notes per voicing.

options.label: Add altered dominants, m7b5 and tritone subs
options.consequence: Most jazz. How often lo-fi uses these is UNVERIFIED, and they feed RL's drift toward chromatic color (SMART).

decisions.question: Can the model write any chord sequence, or does it choose from familiar progression families?

options.label: Any sequence from the vocabulary
options.consequence: Most novelty, but many progressions that don't sound idiomatic. The theory verifier carries the load.

options.label: Free, but the verifier rewards known families
options.consequence: ii-V vamp, I-vi-ii-V, Royal Road, Just the Two of Us, borrowed iv or bVII. Nudges toward idiom.

options.label: A template plus one substitution slot
options.consequence: Almost always idiomatic, with little harmonic search. Creativity moves to melody, bass and drums.

options.label: The brief supplies the progression
options.consequence: Harmony becomes a knob, and the RM learns only melody, bass and drums.

decisions.question: Should loops float, or resolve?

options.label: Float: avoid strong V-I arrivals
options.consequence: Endless and background-friendly. The verifier penalizes cadences.

options.label: Resolve only at the seam (bar 8 leads to the tonic at bar 1)
options.consequence: The loop turns around every cycle. Ties in with the bar-8 policy.

options.label: Functional cadences allowed anywhere
options.consequence: Most song-like, least loop-like.

decisions.question: How should the chords move and be played?

options.label: One chord per bar, held
options.consequence: Pad-like and sleepy, with the fewest notes.

options.label: One chord per bar, with rhythmic stabs on the offbeats
options.consequence: The study-beats Rhodes style. Needs a field for the comping rhythm.

options.label: Two chords in some bars (a ii-V inside one bar)
options.consequence: Jazzhop movement and denser harmony.

options.label: The model chooses each chord's duration and rhythm
options.consequence: Most freedom, but more room to hack (the density drift SMART reported).

decisions.question: What voicing shape should the compiler produce?

options.label: 3-note rootless close voicings, about C3-C5
options.consequence: Airy jazz-piano sound with little mud. The bass supplies the root.

options.label: 4-note close voicings, about C3-C5
options.consequence: Fuller and warmer, with a risk of mud near C3.

options.label: Spread across two octaves
options.consequence: Lush and ballad-like, but clashes more with the lead's register.

options.label: The model picks a voicing style for each chord
options.consequence: The RM can learn your voicing taste. Adds a DSL field and more room to hack.

decisions.question: Between chords, should the voices move smoothly or slide as parallel shapes?

options.label: Automatic smooth voice leading (nearest inversion, shared notes held)
options.consequence: Pianistic and seamless.

options.label: Parallel planing (the same shape slides up or down)
options.consequence: The sound of chopped samples, like Dilla's chords.

options.label: Top voice leads (the compiler keeps the top note moving by step)
options.consequence: The chords carry a hidden melody.

options.label: The model specifies each chord's inversion
options.consequence: More control, and more ways to sound clumsy.

decisions.question: How many out-of-scale notes are allowed, and where?

options.label: In-scale notes only
options.consequence: Safest, and blocks RL's drift toward chromatic notes. Less jazz.

options.label: Chromatic approach notes in the bass only
options.consequence: The jazzy bass habit of notes that surround the target.

options.label: Approach notes in bass and lead, at most 1-2 per bar
options.consequence: Expressive, with a guard against hacking.

options.label: Any accidentals, judged by the verifier
options.consequence: Most expression, and the easiest drift for RL to exploit.

decisions.question: What happens when the lead clashes with the chord (a minor 2nd or b9) on a strong beat?

options.label: Hard gate
options.consequence: Any clash on beat 1 or 3 zeroes the reward. Clean, but may kill tasteful crunch.

options.label: Soft theory penalty
options.consequence: Discouraged, and the penalty fades as the theory weight decays from 0.5 to 0.1.

options.label: Allowed if the next note resolves it by step
options.consequence: The jazz appoggiatura. The verifier needs logic to detect resolution.

options.label: Allowed freely
options.consequence: Crunch is part of the sound, and the RM decides.

decisions.question: How busy may the lead be?

options.label: No lead
options.consequence: A pure bed. Lead instruments leave the palette, and the RM judges only harmony and groove.

options.label: Sparse: one short motif every 2 bars, with rests
options.consequence: Understated. A hard cap on notes per bar guards against RL's drift toward more notes.

options.label: Call and response across 4 bars
options.consequence: Melodic, yet still loop-like.

options.label: A continuous lead line
options.consequence: Hook-first and the least background-friendly. Still needs a density cap.

decisions.question: Who chooses the instruments, and from how many options per role?

options.label: One fixed band in the palette
options.consequence: Votes judge the writing and there is no timbre to hack. Smallest audition job.

options.label: The model picks from 2-3 options per role
options.consequence: The RM can learn which sounds you like, but votes become partly about timbre.

options.label: The brief names the instruments from the list
options.consequence: Instrument choice becomes part of knob obedience, and two loops for the same brief share a band.

options.label: The model picks freely from 10+ instruments
options.consequence: Most variety, the biggest confound, and the most audition and licensing work.

decisions.question: Should the two loops in a vote use the same instruments, so you judge the writing and not the timbre?

options.label: Always the same instruments
options.consequence: The RM learns composition. You set timbre directly in the palette.

options.label: Usually the same (about 80/20)
options.consequence: The RM also learns some timbre preference.

options.label: Random, no matching
options.consequence: Your likes and dislikes of instruments may drive the votes, and the RM risks becoming an instrument detector.

changes: seed-pool generator (several loops per instrument set)

decisions.question: What bass sound and what kind of bass line?

options.label: Upright pizz, holding the root through each chord
options.consequence: Sleepy or jazzhop. The simplest line.

options.label: Electric finger bass: root, fifth and chromatic approach notes
options.consequence: Chillhop movement.

options.label: A sine-like sub doubling the roots sparsely
options.consequence: Boom-bap minimalism.

options.label: Walking quarter notes on upright
options.consequence: Jazzier and busier, with more density risk.

decisions.question: Should the bass lock to the kick?

options.label: Bass notes start with the kicks
options.consequence: Tight and punchy, and suits sidechain.

options.label: Independent and held
options.consequence: Floaty and sleepy.

options.label: Anticipates the bar by an 8th or a 16th
options.consequence: Pushes forward. Jazzy.

options.label: No rule, the RM decides
options.consequence: Fewer verifiers, but the RM must learn this from about 1,500 votes.

decisions.question: Which drum kit, and which drum voices are on the list?

options.label: Minimal: kick, snare, closed hat
options.consequence: Few pieces at once. The simplest audition.

options.label: Chillhop: soft kick, rim or cross-stick backbeat, closed hat, shaker
options.consequence: Suits ghost notes. Sources: VCSL and Virtuosity, both CC0.

options.label: Brushes/jazz: soft kick, brush snare with stirs, ride, no hats
options.consequence: Sleepy or jazzhop. Karoryfer Swirly is CC0 but 1.7 GB, so extract only the hits you need.

options.label: Boom-bap: harder kick, dusty snare with a short plate, swung hats, an occasional open hat cut off by the closed hat
options.consequence: The most energy.

decisions.question: Does the model write raw drum grids, or pick from grooves you approved?

options.label: Free step grid for each drum
options.consequence: The model can discover grooves, but produces the most junk, and the RM must learn your groove taste.

options.label: Free grids plus a backbone check (kick on 1, snare on 2 and 4, cap on hat density)
options.consequence: An idiomatic floor with room above it.

options.label: Pick from 8-12 groove templates you approve, plus a fill slot
options.consequence: You fix the groove taste by hand. Creativity moves to harmony and melody.

options.label: The brief picks the groove
options.consequence: Drums leave the model's control.

decisions.question: Which hat grid, and ghost notes or not?

options.label: Straight 8th-note hats, no ghost notes
options.consequence: Calm and suits sleepy loops.

options.label: 16th-note hats with accents (on-beats loudest, off-beats softer)
options.consequence: Busier chillhop movement.

options.label: Shaker-led 16ths with sparse hats
options.consequence: Softer top end.

options.label: 8th-note hats plus very soft snare ghost notes around the backbeat
options.consequence: Boom-bap groove. Needs soft ghost-note samples.

decisions.question: Is the 'machine-gun' effect (the identical sample on every hit) a dealbreaker for you?

options.label: One sample per drum
options.consequence: Simplest and true to sampled loops, but can sound mechanical.

options.label: Fixed rotation of 2-4 samples per drum
options.consequence: More natural and still bit-identical. More audition work.

options.label: Soft and hard sample layers for snare and hats
options.consequence: Ghost notes sound like real ghost notes.

options.label: Both the rotation and the soft/hard layers
options.consequence: Most natural, and the most palette work.

decisions.question: What rhythmic grid can the model write on?

options.label: 16 steps per bar, with swing added by the renderer
options.consequence: Simple, but no triplets or flams.

options.label: 16 steps plus small per-step nudges, within limits
options.consequence: The model can push and pull hits, so it can learn feel, and also hack it.

options.label: 24 steps per bar (allows triplets)
options.consequence: Triplets are written out, so the renderer must not add its swing on top.

options.label: 32 steps per bar
options.consequence: Hat rolls and flams. Close to trap, probably not your taste.

decisions.question: How many layers can play at once?

options.label: 3 (drums, bass, chords), with a lead allowed only in A'
options.consequence: Sparse and background-friendly.

options.label: 4 (drums, bass, chords, lead)
options.consequence: Standard.

options.label: 5 (add a pad or counter-melody)
options.consequence: Lush, with more masking and mud.

options.label: The model chooses, up to 5, capped by a verifier
options.consequence: The RM decides. Note that Audiobox PC literally rewards more parts.

decisions.question: What shape should the 8 bars take, and how much literal repetition is good?

options.label: A 2- or 4-bar cell, repeated
options.consequence: The most loop-like. The '>3 identical bars' penalty must be loosened or redefined.

options.label: A (bars 1-4) then A' (bars 5-8) with small changes
options.consequence: The usual default, and fits the penalty as written.

options.label: A then a contrasting B in bars 5-8
options.consequence: More song-like, less hypnotic.

options.label: Every bar different
options.consequence: The least loop-like, and may get tiring on repeat.

decisions.question: What does bar 8 do by default, as enforced by the verifier?

options.label: Must stay plain
options.consequence: Repeats seamlessly and suits background listening. No fill syntax needed.

options.label: A fill or drop-out is allowed but not required
options.consequence: The RM learns whether you like them.

options.label: Turnaround harmony required (V7alt, bII7, or ii-V back to bar 1)
options.consequence: The verifier checks it, giving a cadence every cycle.

options.label: Drum variation or drop-out required
options.consequence: Marks the loop point, but risks sounding formulaic.

decisions.question: Do you judge loops as they repeat, or as a single pass?

options.label: Always heard looped (two cycles)
options.consequence: You judge the seam where bar 8 returns to bar 1. The renderer must wrap note tails and keep the LFOs and bed periodic.

options.label: Single pass
options.consequence: Faster votes, but the seam is never judged or learned.

options.label: Votes on a single pass; ear checks and the final A/B looped
options.consequence: The seam is checked but not rewarded.

changes: renderer (two-cycle render, tail wrap, bed crossfade)

decisions.question: Can a nearly empty loop (a few notes over pleasant rain) pass?

options.label: Hard minimum-content gate (each core part plays in at least N bars)
options.consequence: Blocks a 'rain plus silence' hack, but rules out near-empty ambient loops.

options.label: Soft penalty for empty bars
options.consequence: Discouraged but still possible.

options.label: Allowed; your votes decide
options.consequence: If you vote sparse loops up, the model may drift there. Log it as a hack signature.

decisions.question: What does 'fine' mean in the Phase 1 ear check of 50 clips, where at least 30% must be fine?

options.label: I'd leave it playing while I study
options.consequence: Strict and tied to the loop's job, so the SFT fallback is more likely to trigger.

options.label: Nothing makes me skip it on the first listen
options.consequence: A lenient floor that is easy to reach.

options.label: Scores 3 or more on a 1-5 scale
options.consequence: Produces absolute labels you can reuse for the 'pairwise vs absolute' ablation.

decisions.question: How loud is the rain bed relative to the music? (It is set relative before normalizing to -14 LUFS, so sparse loops don't end up with louder rain.)

options.label: -30 dB
options.consequence: Felt rather than heard.

options.label: -24 dB
options.consequence: Present on headphones, gone on speakers.

options.label: -18 dB
options.consequence: Clearly audible rain.

options.label: -12 dB
options.consequence: A featured texture that masks quiet parts and colors both votes and CLAP.

decisions.question: What kind of rain?

options.label: Light rain on a window, heard from inside (Freesound 161705, 37.6 s, mono)
options.consequence: Intimate. It has hits on an air-conditioner unit to edit out, and is short, so it needs crossfades to hide repetition.

options.label: Soft rain on a roof window (Freesound 235827, 3:16, 48 kHz/24-bit stereo)
options.consequence: Rich and wide. Pick excerpts that avoid its birdsong and thunder.

options.label: Steady, heavier rain
options.consequence: Masks more. A CC0 source still has to be found and checked.

options.label: Rain with occasional distant thunder
options.consequence: Dramatic, but thunder falls on different bars in each loop and can sway individual votes.

changes: assets (CC0 originals + manifest with URL, author, license, SHA256)

decisions.question: Does every loop get the same rain excerpt, or a different one chosen deterministically?

options.label: The same excerpt everywhere
options.consequence: Perfectly constant within pairs, but you will hear the same raindrops about 3,000+ times over 1,500 votes.

options.label: Excerpt chosen by the brief
options.consequence: Two loops for the same brief share the rain. The harness must write the bed offset into the LoopScript header so the same LoopScript still gives the same WAV.

options.label: Excerpt chosen by a hash of the LoopScript
options.consequence: Most variety, but differences in the bed add noise inside every pair.

decisions.question: Vinyl crackle or tape hiss on top of the rain?

options.label: None, rain only
options.consequence: Cleaner, closer to chillhop.

options.label: Subtle crackle (synthesized random clicks, or CC0 Freesound 471007, with a whole number of 1.8 s record turns per loop)
options.consequence: Classic lo-fi warmth.

options.label: Featured crackle with pops
options.consequence: Deliberately dusty, but it competes with the rain.

options.label: Tape hiss only (CC0 Freesound 443338)
options.consequence: Cassette character instead of vinyl.

decisions.question: How dark is the master bus: where does the low-pass filter start? (Assumes a steep 24 dB/oct filter, because pedalboard's LowpassFilter is only 6 dB/oct.)

options.label: About 6 kHz
options.consequence: Very dark, like a cassette.

options.label: About 8 kHz
options.consequence: Dark and warm.

options.label: About 10 kHz
options.consequence: Gently rolled off.

options.label: 12 kHz or higher
options.consequence: Clean, leaning toward chillhop.

decisions.question: How much tape wobble in pitch (wow and flutter)? Real consumer decks measure 0.05-0.10%, and plugins exaggerate this.

options.label: None
options.consequence: Steady pitch, so held Rhodes chords stay in tune.

options.label: Subtle: 0.1% peak (about 1.7 cents) at about 0.5 Hz
options.consequence: Warmth you feel more than hear.

options.label: Obvious: 0.3% (about 5 cents)
options.consequence: Classic seasick tape.

options.label: Heavy: 1% (about 17 cents)
options.consequence: A deliberate warble that sours held chords.

decisions.question: How much digital grit from bit-depth and sample-rate reduction?

options.label: Clean
options.consequence: Modern and hi-fi.

options.label: Gentle tape-style saturation only
options.consequence: Warmth without crunch. pedalboard Distortion's default 25 dB drive is far too hot.

options.label: SP-1200-style crush (12-bit, 26.04 kHz) on the drums only
options.consequence: Dusty drums over clean keys, with aliasing from the cheap resampling.

options.label: The same crush on the whole mix
options.consequence: The most lo-fi, with harsh aliasing on the keys.

decisions.question: Sidechain pumping?

options.label: None
options.consequence: A static mix.

options.label: Subtle: the kick ducks chords and bass by 1-2 dB
options.consequence: Glues the mix.

options.label: Obvious: the whole mix pumps, rain included
options.consequence: The classic breathing lo-fi sound.

options.label: Duck only the rain bed
options.consequence: The rain breathes with the kick while the music stays steady.

changes: renderer (deterministic sidechain from the kick lane)

decisions.question: What space does the loop sit in? (FluidSynth's built-in reverb and chorus get turned off; all reverb comes from pedalboard or a CC0 impulse response.)

options.label: Dry or a small room
options.consequence: Intimate, like a bedroom.

options.label: Short plate on the snare, small room on the keys
options.consequence: Boom-bap.

options.label: Vintage spring or plate sound on the keys
options.consequence: Classic lo-fi.

options.label: Large, washy space
options.consequence: Dreamy, but producers warn against cathedral-sized tails.

decisions.question: Which part sits on top, and how wide is the mix?

options.label: Keys on top, drums tucked in, close to mono
options.consequence: Background-friendly, like radio.

options.label: Drums and bass forward, keys behind
options.consequence: Head-nod.

options.label: Lead forward
options.consequence: Hook-first.

options.label: Keys and pads wide, drums and bass centred
options.consequence: Lush on headphones, thinner on laptop speakers.

decisions.question: Which licenses can committed palette assets have, given the repo may go public?

options.label: CC0 or public domain only
options.consequence: The cleanest repo (FreePats, VCSL, VSCO2 CE, Virtuosity, Freesound CC0), but no sampled Rhodes, felt piano, muted trumpet, celesta or music box.

options.label: Also permissive custom licenses and CC-BY, with an ATTRIBUTION file
options.consequence: GeneralUser GS, Greg Sullivan E-Pianos, YDP Grand, MSLP Vibes and MuldjordKit cover nearly every role.

options.label: Also non-commercial assets, downloaded by script and never committed
options.consequence: Allows jRhodes3d (CC-BY-NC). The repo is no longer self-contained and needs a fetch script with SHA256 checks.

options.label: Also GPL SoundFonts
options.consequence: TimGM6mb (GPL-2) and FreePats GM (GPL-3+) bring copyleft obligations into a public repo.

decisions.question: Which electric piano? (This is the weakest spot for licensing.)

options.label: GeneralUser GS Tine EP
options.consequence: Permissive, about 30 MB, can be committed. General-MIDI-grade realism, and its author can't vouch for where every sample came from.

options.label: Greg Sullivan Wurlitzer EP200 (CC-BY 3.0)
options.consequence: A barkier Wurlitzer tone. Needs SFZ-to-SF2 conversion with Polyphone, plus attribution.

options.label: jRhodes3d, a 1977 Mk I (CC-BY-NC, download-only)
options.consequence: The most realistic Rhodes, with up to 5 velocity layers, but it can't be committed.

options.label: FM electric piano (FreePats, or VCSL TX81Z; CC0)
options.consequence: 80s DX7 character, not a Rhodes.

decisions.question: Can tracks from your own library serve as private references, never committed?

options.label: Names only, no audio
options.consequence: Taste comes in only through words and votes.

options.label: Private A/B on the laptop, loudness-matched against palette renders
options.consequence: Tunes timbre and darkness against real records, and nothing leaves the laptop.

options.label: The above, plus embeddings of the reference tracks as a prior for the RM
options.consequence: A stronger prior, but copyrighted audio would sit on cluster scratch. Check policy first.

decisions.question: What must pass before palette_v1 freezes on Nov 8?

plan_facts.fact: Noise ceiling: if two of Shresth's votes on the same pair agree with probability p, the best possible RM agreement is q = (1+sqrt(2p-1))/2. Reaching 70% needs p >= 0.58 (p=0.65 gives 0.77, p=0.80 gives 0.89). Measure repeat agreement in week 1.
plan_facts.source: Taste report section A4 (derivation); context https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.01325

plan_facts.fact: Precision: 200 held-out votes at 70% have a 95% CI of about +/-6.4 pp. The 100-brief final A/B has about +/-9 pp. 100-150 repeated pairs estimate p within about +/-7-9 pp.
Pairs of samples from the same RL policy are the hardest pairs: researcher-researcher agreement was about 65%, and about 80% on the easiest pairs. Low-confidence votes were still worth keeping.
Intra-rater consistency falls on single-genre material: rho 0.80 on 5-genre material vs 0.38 on single-genre material, same raters two weeks apart. Mood mattered.

Data scale for preference RMs: TuneJury reached 70.9% with 17.5k pairs and 66.8% with 5.1k (frozen CLAP + MERT-330M, 2.8M-parameter MLP); concatenating CLAP and MERT gave no gain. MusicRL reached 60% with 285k crowd pairs. Text RMs stayed near chance below about 2k comparisons.

Listening time at 80 BPM (24 s loops): 1,500 full loops played A then B take about 23 h (about 55 sessions of 25 min). 10 s synced excerpts take about 10 h (about 25 sessions). 300 best-worst-of-4 tuples take about 5.4 h.
BS.1116-3: sessions of at most 20-30 min with about 10-15 trials, and rest at least as long as the session. Switching should be near-instant (about 40 ms) and click-free, and order randomized.

BS.1534-3 (MUSHRA): excerpts of about 10 s (preferably at most 12 s), 5 ms raised-cosine fades on every switch, no cross-fades, loudness aligned before the test, and listener level adjustment within 4 dB.

MusicRL: users compared 20 s clips, and RM accuracy fell from 60% to 56% when inputs were cut to 3-5 s. Its user-preference RM was over-optimized in under 2,000 steps even at KL 0.001. Quality predicted user preference only 53.3% of the time, and text adherence 51.6%.

Train the expanded pairs of one ranking as a single batch element (shuffling them as independent examples overfit InstructGPT's RM). BWS-4 implies 5 of 6 pairs and beat rating scales at small budgets. Rao-Kupper BT-with-ties beat plain BT on data with ties.

webMUSHRA provides sample-accurate Web Audio looping and switching, AB/ABX/paired modes, and YAML config. With a fixed tempo every loop shares one bar grid, so toggling between A and B at the same bar position is trivial.

Audiobox Aesthetics scores PQ, PC, CE and CU on 16 kHz mono audio in 10 s windows. PC literally measures how many components are mixed together. Training used no synthetic audio. The PyPI package is audiobox_aesthetics 0.0.4.

SMART (TRL GRPO, Audiobox CE reward, beta 0.04, 8 prompts x 8 completions, 200 iterations) produced more notes, more polyphony, wider pitch range, more chromaticism and fewer empty beats. A long beta=0 run collapsed diversity. Changing the renderer alone moved mean CE by more than 1 point (5.42 vs 6.60).
Optimizing Audiobox PQ alone raised every Audiobox score by about 10% while an independent alignment check dropped (verifier hacking).

HF laion/larger_clap_music uses 48 kHz, a 10 s maximum, truncation=rand_trunc (a random crop) and padding=repeatpad. Loops of 21-27 s therefore get nondeterministic embeddings unless they are chunked into fixed, bar-aligned windows of at most 10 s.
CLAP barely encodes negation, and CLAPScore correlates weakly with human ratings. The constant rain bed may saturate rain themes (hypothesis), so consider scoring CLAP on a render without the bed.

MERT v1-95M and v1-330M are CC-BY-NC-4.0, take 24 kHz input at 75 frames/s, need trust_remote_code, and break on transformers >=4.44 unless config.conv_pos_batch_norm=False is set. vLLM 0.32.0 pins transformers >=5.16.1,<5.20.0, so the scorer environment must be planned separately.

The laion_clap music checkpoint music_audioset_epoch_15_esc_90.14.pt needs amodel='HTSAT-base', enable_fusion=False and 48 kHz input, and loading may require stripping a position_ids key. The kit's fetch job does not download *.pt files, so this checkpoint needs another fetch path.

TRL 1.17.1 needs Python >=3.11 and vLLM >=0.22.1,<0.33. GRPOConfig defaults: use_vllm=False, vllm_mode=colocate, num_generations=8, max_completion_length=512, beta=0.0 (no KL and no reference model), loss_type=dapo, scale_rewards=group, temperature 1.0.

reward_weights are static, so the curriculum (theory 0.5 to 0.1, taste 0.2 to 0.6) must be computed inside the reward functions from trainer_state.global_step. A function that returns None is excluded for that sample, and each function logs rewards/<name>/mean and std.

Sampling with top_p<1, top_k>0 or min_p>0 biases the vLLM importance-sampling correction, unless running in colocate mode on vLLM >=0.28 with top_k>0. vllm_structured_outputs_regex can enforce LoopScript syntax; how it interacts with the IS correction is unverified.

LoRA for RL: rank 1-32 on all linear layers is enough, with a learning rate of about 1e-5 (about 10x full fine-tuning) and an effective batch below about 32. With PEFT, the reference model is the base with the adapter disabled.

Mitigations for reward over-optimization with evidence behind them: worst-case or uncertainty-weighted ensembles (better across different backbones than across seeds), a bounded centered reward sigmoid(r - r_ref) (PAR), and refreshing preferences on the current policy each round (Llama 2).

Base models: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (dense, non-thinking, Apache-2.0, IFEval 83.4) and Granite 4.1 8B (dense, Apache-2.0, IFEval 87.06) are the lowest risk. Qwen3.5-4B is a hybrid Gated-DeltaNet model with vision that thinks by default. Ministral 3 8B recommends temperature below 0.1.

MPC swing is the share of each 8th-note pair given to the first 16th: 50% is straight, 66% about triplet, 75% the maximum. Linn: 54% loosens a beat without sounding swung, and at 90 BPM 62% feels looser than 66%. The even 16th is delayed by (s-0.5) x 30/BPM s, so 58% at 80 BPM is 30 ms. On the FL/Cubase scale, 0% = MPC 50% and 100% = MPC 66.6%.

Dilla's offsets repeated identically, many times per song; they were not random. Perceived onset depends on the sound, so microtiming should be a fixed offset per instrument and per layer, not random jitter on each hit.

An 8-bar loop lasts L = 1920/BPM s (24 s at 80 BPM, 21.3 s at 90). A seamless loop needs tails wrapped (render two cycles and keep the second), every LFO at f = k/L, and noise beds crossfaded at the seam.

Pin FluidSynth 2.6.1 on both machines. Version 2.6.0 changed sample fine-tuning (flagged as musically breaking), made Dattorro the default reverb and dropped 7th-order sinc interpolation. Homebrew and conda-forge are both at 2.6.1.

FluidSynth chorus and reverb are on by default (synth.chorus.active=1, synth.reverb.active=1) and must be turned off; synth.gain defaults to 0.2. Events are processed in 64-sample blocks (about 1.45 ms at 44.1 kHz), while the numpy drum sampler is sample-accurate.

pyfluidsynth get_samples() goes through fluid_synth_write_s16, which dithers with an index that persists across calls, so a reused synth's output depends on what it rendered before. Render float output with a fresh or reset synth per render, effects off and cpu-cores=1, and parallelize across processes.
FluidSynth has no SFZ loader, and sfizz was archived on 2026-06-21. Convert SFZ to SF2 offline with the Polyphone CLI.

pedalboard 0.9.26: LowpassFilter and HighpassFilter are first-order (6 dB/oct). Limiter applies makeup gain and hard-clips. BrickwallLimiter with true_peak exists since 0.9.25. Distortion's default drive of 25 dB is very hot. Resample with ZeroOrderHold aliases, which suits SP-1200 emulation. Plugins that buffer can return fewer samples, so check output length.

pyloudnorm normalize.loudness is pure gain (no limiting, no true-peak handling). Procedure: set the bed relative to the music's LUFS, sum, gain to -14 LUFS, apply a true-peak brickwall at about -1 dB, then re-measure up to 3 times to within +/-0.1 LU. Input must be float, shaped (samples, channels).

numpy Generator streams and SIMD code paths can differ across builds and CPUs. Use an integer-hash PRNG (such as SplitMix64) for humanize timing, crackle and drift, pin numpy, and make canonical renders on one node type.

Byte-identical outputs differed between arm64 laptops and x86 nodes even with bitexact flags. The cluster render must be the canonical one, and laptop listening clips should be cluster renders pulled back.

GitHub blocks files over 100 MiB and warns at 50 MiB. Fetch FluidR3_GM sf2 (141 MB), MuseScore_General sf2 (208 MB) and Salamander (296 MiB) by script; commit GeneralUser GS (about 30 MB), MuseScore_General sf3 (35.9 MB) and the small FreePats SF2s.

The GeneralUser GS v2.0.3 license allows use in software and modification, with no attribution required. The author asks people not to hotlink his downloads and says he cannot be fully sure where every sample came from. It includes Tine EP, FM EP and the Jazz (32) and Brush (40) drum programs.

No CC0 sampled Rhodes, felt piano, muted trumpet, celesta or music box was found. jRhodes3d samples are CC-BY-NC-4.0 (fetch only). Greg Sullivan E-Pianos (Wurlitzer EP200, CP80, Pianet T) are CC-BY 3.0.

CC0 options exist for most roles: FreePats upright piano, nylon guitar, clean jazz guitar, electric bass, tenor sax, pads and FM EP; VCSL and VSCO2 CE vibraphone, contrabass pizz, flute and percussion; Virtuosity Drums (1.1 GB) and Karoryfer Swirly brushes (1.7 GB), from which the needed hits should be extracted.

Do not commit Arachno (reproduction forbidden), 99Sounds (no redistribution), Pianobook, Looperman or commercial packs. Gogodze Phu Vol II is CC0 according to sfzinstruments but GPL-3 according to KVR, so check the bundled license.

Freesound serves original files only through OAuth2 (token access gives lossy previews), so commit the CC0 originals with a manifest of URL, author, license and SHA256. Rain candidates: 161705 (37.6 s, mono, with air-conditioner hits) and 235827 (3:16, 48 kHz/24-bit, with birdsong and distant thunder).
Practitioners put crackle and rain about 18-30 dB below the main elements (weak sources). Heavy, deliberate texture goes up to -12 to -8 dB.

Drum realism: accent beat 1 hardest, then 3, then 2 and 4, and vary the hats most. Flat velocities, copy-pasted hats and the same velocity pattern every bar sound fake. Round robins and velocity layers fix the machine-gun effect.
Low-interval limits: a major third goes muddy below about B1-D#2, and close voicings below C3 tend to be muddy. Rootless voicings need the root to sound in the bass.
CLAUDE.md forbids training on the laptop, so active pair selection needs either an explicit exception or a pair queue built nightly on the cluster.
The Phase 4 ablations (pairwise vs absolute; palette vs free-form; curriculum on/off) need absolute ratings and a free-form grammar, which nothing else in the plan produces.

Pre-registered final claims: in a blind A/B on 100 held-out briefs Shresth picks step-N over step-0 at least 70% of the time; knob obedience is at least 90%; within-group mean embedding distance stays at least 70% of its step-0 value.

Measure quality automatically on a small sample before asking a human to rate. Small models ignore format constraints, so use a deterministic repair stage that logs every repair, record finish_reason, and set sampling parameters explicitly (default sampling gave near-identical samples).
The kit's approval format is a line of its own matching ^APPROVED by <Name> <YYYY-MM-DD>$. It can record ear-check and palette-freeze approvals.

The kit's budget guard conflicts with CLAUDE.md. Its default max_project_sus is 250000, against the 1,000,000 SU target. It requires job names prefixed with the project name, but CLAUDE.md names jobs 'lofi-<purpose>'. It needs absolute --output log paths, but CLAUDE.md uses relative logs/%x_%j.out. A GPU job without -c/--mem is costed at 104 SU/min.

bootstrap.sh refuses any non-empty target, so it cannot run in /Users/shresthrana/csci596-project, where CLAUDE.md already exists. Bootstrap into a fresh directory and copy pieces over, or move CLAUDE.md aside first.
Project storage is /project2/<account> (1 TB shared by the class), not /project as CLAUDE.md:25 says. Scratch is about 10 TB and purged, and job $TMPDIR is a 126 GB tmpfs.

Discovery 'CPUs' are hardware threads: an EPYC 7542 is 32 cores / 64 threads, and render efficiency was 96/94/89/74/49% at 4/8/16/32/64 workers. A100 nodes hold 2 GPUs. Both shape the 16-to-256-core and 1-to-4-GPU scaling claims. A big render sweep should be one job with a worker pool, not a job array.

Known-good on Discovery: vllm 0.32.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, driver 580 (CUDA 13). Compute nodes have outbound internet. No text-only instruct model has been verified there. The debug partition is one 2xA40 node that is often drained.

CLAUDE.md's make pull (runs/*/summary/ into runs/) merges same-named files from different runs. Its .rsyncignore omits logs/, opt/, jobs/submissions.log and checkpoint directories, which rsync --delete would then remove on the cluster.

risks: Listening hours overrun the Phase 2 window. About 1,500 votes on ~24 s clips take ~10 h with 10 s synced excerpts and ~23 h with full sequential A/B, which is 1.5-3.3 h/day across Nov 9-15. That is before adding triage (0.3-4 h), hidden repeats (+5-15%), anchors, Phase 1 auditions and ear checks (10 loops, the 50-clip gate, any stress set), nightly votes, the final 100-brief A/B (~40-90 min) and any by-ear ablations. BS.1116 fatigue limits (20-30 min sessions with equal rest) make more than about 1.5 h/day hard to sustain.

The 70% RM target may be at or above Shresth's own consistency ceiling. Reaching it needs repeat agreement of at least 58%. Researchers agreed only about 65% on pairs from the same policy, single-genre material roughly halved intra-rater consistency, and 200 held-out votes carry +/-6.4 pp.

1,500 votes is thin by published standards. Population music-preference RMs needed 5k-17.5k pairs to reach 67-71%, and text RMs stayed near chance below about 2k comparisons. Plan for a low-capacity head, learning curves at 200/400/800 votes, and a possible miss of the target.

Votes and RM embeddings are tied to palette_v1 renders. Any change after the freeze, or pilot votes taken before the Nov 8 freeze, invalidates those labels. Phase 1 must also fit the DSL, compiler, renderer, SFZ-to-SF2 conversions, license checks, auditions, 10 approved loops and the 500-sample gate into 7 days.

Licensing gaps. No CC0 sampled Rhodes, felt piano, muted trumpet, celesta or music box exists. jRhodes3d is non-commercial (fetch-only, so the public repo is not self-contained). Gogodze Phu has conflicting licenses, and GeneralUser's author cannot vouch for every sample. Several Freesound items were checked as CC0 only via the search filter, not on their pages. MERT is CC-BY-NC, which limits publishing anything derived from its weights. Private reference audio must never be committed.

Bit-identity will probably fail between arm64 macOS and x86 Rocky (FluidSynth, pedalboard, numpy SIMD). Within one machine, pyfluidsynth's dithered s16 path makes output depend on render order, FluidSynth effects are on by default, buffering plugins change output length, and CLAP's rand_trunc crops randomly. Canonical renders must therefore come from one cluster node type, so every laptop listening batch needs a pull and a Duo session.

The scorers may work against the lo-fi aesthetic. A CE reward under GRPO drove denser, more chromatic output and diversity collapse, and PC rewards more components. Audiobox never saw synthetic audio and shifts by more than 1 point with the renderer, and optimizing PQ hacked an independent check. CLAP is weak, misses negation, and may be saturated by the constant rain bed.

Over-optimization can arrive fast. A music user-preference RM was gamed in under 2,000 steps even with KL 0.001. TRL now defaults to beta=0 (no KL), and group-std reward scaling amplifies RM noise when completions are similar.

The scorer and training environments conflict. MERT's remote code breaks on transformers >=4.44, while vLLM 0.32 needs transformers 5.16-5.19. laion_clap needs a checkpoint patch, and the kit's fetch job skips its .pt file. Scorers may need their own environment, which costs env-build SU: the kit's serve-env build alone can reach 1,440 SU, above the 500 SU ask-first rule.

Votes can pick up confounds. If instruments, tempo, key or the rain excerpt differ within a pair, votes may reflect timbre or tempo likes rather than the writing. An identical rain excerpt heard thousands of times may fatigue or annoy the listener.

Excerpts can hide structure. A 10 s excerpt (about 3.3 bars at 80 BPM) never contains bar 8 or the loop seam unless the window is chosen deliberately, so turnarounds, fills and seams get no reward signal.
Near-empty loops over a pleasant, constant rain bed might score well with the RM or Audiobox (an inferred hack). Without a minimum-content gate the policy could drift toward sparse ambience.

The single-listener evaluation is open to bias. One person writes the briefs, picks checkpoints and judges. After ~1,500 Phase 2 votes he may recognize step-0 style, which weakens blinding, and selecting checkpoints on his votes or the tie rule can inflate the 70% claim.

Process friction. Duo means every cluster round-trip needs Shresth to open the ssh master, so a nightly vote-and-refresh loop needs him every day. Most training and env-build jobs exceed the 500 SU ask-first threshold.

Kit and CLAUDE.md conflicts must be settled before Phase 0 ends: /project vs /project2; lofi- vs lofi-rl- job names; relative log paths the guard will not create; the 250k vs 1M SU cap; git rev-parse on compute nodes; rsync --delete removing cluster-only files; make pull flattening run summaries; and bootstrap refusing the non-empty project directory.

Scaling claims rest on wrong hardware assumptions. The '64-core' main nodes are 64 hardware threads (32 cores), and A100 nodes hold 2 GPUs, so a 1-to-4 GPU step-time study needs multi-node runs or L40S nodes.

Base-model risk. Qwen3.5's hybrid layers have unverified training kernels and think by default, and Ministral recommends temperature below 0.1 while GRPO samples at 1.0. No benchmark measures DSL strictness, and constrained decoding's interaction with the IS correction is unverified.

The frontier seed pool carries the frontier model's style. If it is used for SFT, the near-copy penalty starts to bind. Provider terms on training models with their outputs also need checking; the reports do not cover this.

The GPU queue may delay early milestones. The debug partition is a single 2xA40 node that is often drained, and GPU waits depend on other jobs' age, so smoke_env and the Phase 2 GRPO smoke test may slip.
Taste drift and mood. Preferences shift across days and moods, so votes spread over 5+ weeks may not be stationary. Without repeat pairs and a recency rule, the RM chases a moving target.
